"'''Every Morning'''" is a song by American [[rock music|rock]] band [[Sugar Ray]], released as the [[lead single]] from their third studio album, ''[[14:59]]'' (1999). The track is an [[alternative rock]] and [[flamenco pop]] song that references [[Malo (band)|Malo]]'s "[[Suavecito (Malo song)|Suavecito]]" and [[Hugh Masekela]]'s "[[Grazing in the Grass]]". Serviced to US radio in December 1998, "Every Morning" was physically released in Japan in January 1999 and in the United States that March, making it Sugar Ray's first commercially available single in the US.<ref name="spotlight"/>

"Every Morning" reached number one on both the US ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Modern Rock Tracks]] chart and the Canadian ''[[RPM (magazine)|RPM]]'' 100 Hit Tracks chart, becoming Canada's second-most successful single of 1999. The song also reached number three on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and number 10 on the [[UK Singles Chart]], becoming the band's highest-charting single on both rankings.

"Every Morning" is a song by American rock band Sugar Ray, released as the lead single from their third studio album, 14:59 (1999). The track is an alternative rock and flamenco pop song that references Malo's "Suavecito" and Hugh Masekela's "Grazing in the Grass". Serviced to US radio in December 1998, "Every Morning" was physically released in Japan in January 1999 and in the United States that March, making it Sugar Ray's first commercially available single in the US.

"Every Morning" reached number one on both the US Billboard Modern Rock Tracks chart and the Canadian RPM 100 Hit Tracks chart, becoming Canada's second-most successful single of 1999. The song also reached number three on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 10 on the UK Singles Chart, becoming the band's highest-charting single on both rankings.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: "Every Morning" is an [[alternative rock]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://diffuser.fm/1999-alt-rock-videos/|title=Top 10 Alt-Rock Videos from 1999|work=Diffuser.fm|date=March 15, 2014 |access-date=November 4, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://consequence.net/2017/07/ranking-every-alternative-rock-hit-from-worst-to-best/5/|title=Ranking: Every Alternative Rock No. 1 Hit from Worst to Best|last=Cosores|first=Philip|website=[[Consequence of Sound]]|date=July 4, 2017|access-date=December 29, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.com/2019/07/best-alt-rock-songs-1999-list/7/|title=The 69 Best Alternative Rock Songs of 1999|website=[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]|date=July 25, 2019|access-date=January 13, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ygelsias |first1=Matthew |title=The Ultimate Nineties Alt-Rock Playlist |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/politics/archive/2007/05/the-ultimate-nineties-alt-rock-playlist/40279/ |website=The Atlantic|date=21 May 2007 }}</ref> and [[flamenco pop]] song.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/510116/sugar-ray-beat-one-hit-wonder-jinx-with-new-single/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201028085313/http://www.mtv.com/news/510116/sugar-ray-beat-one-hit-wonder-jinx-with-new-single/|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 28, 2020|title=Sugar Ray Beat One-Hit-Wonder Jinx with New Single|website=[[MTV]] }}</ref> It is written in [[common time]] with a key of [[A-flat major|A{{music|flat}} major]] and proceeds at a moderate tempo, played ''[[Dynamics (music)|mezzo-forte]]''. The song has a [[chord progression]] of A{{music|flat}}–D{{music|flat}}–A{{music|flat}}–D{{music|flat}}–E{{music|flat}}5.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0101213|title=Every Morning by Sugar Ray – Digital Sheet Music|website=Musicnotes.com|date=March 6, 2012 |id=MN0101213|access-date=February 10, 2022}}</ref> The chorus of the song references "[[Suavecito (Malo song)|Suavecito]]" by the Chicano music group [[Malo (band)|Malo]], as well as [[Hugh Masekela]]'s 1968 hit "[[Grazing in the Grass]]". Lead vocalist [[Mark McGrath]] explained, "We referenced 'Suavecito' because growing up in California, you know, that was just like the low rider anthem. Any car show or swap meet you'd ever go by, you'd always hear that [song] and that just stuck in your mind." He added, "We actually came up with that part, and it was very similar to Malo's part. We were sort of imitating it, and then we said, 'Let's just leave it, we're gonna change it later.' It really makes the song – we think – so we just left it."<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1434704/sugar-ray-coasts-lowriding-groove-every-morning.jhtml | archive-url=https://archive.today/20120905100542/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1434704/sugar-ray-coasts-lowriding-groove-every-morning.jhtml | url-status=dead | archive-date=September 5, 2012 | title=Sugar Ray Coasts Low-Riding Groove For "Every Morning" | publisher=[[MTV]] | date=January 26, 1999 | access-date=December 23, 2011}}</ref>
sections.text: "Every Morning" is an alternative rock and flamenco pop song. It is written in common time with a key of A{{music|flat}} major and proceeds at a moderate tempo, played mezzo-forte. The song has a chord progression of A{{music|flat}}–D{{music|flat}}–A{{music|flat}}–D{{music|flat}}–E{{music|flat}}5. The chorus of the song references "Suavecito" by the Chicano music group Malo, as well as Hugh Masekela's 1968 hit "Grazing in the Grass". Lead vocalist Mark McGrath explained, "We referenced 'Suavecito' because growing up in California, you know, that was just like the low rider anthem. Any car show or swap meet you'd ever go by, you'd always hear that [song] and that just stuck in your mind." He added, "We actually came up with that part, and it was very similar to Malo's part. We were sort of imitating it, and then we said, 'Let's just leave it, we're gonna change it later.' It really makes the song – we think – so we just left it."

sections.heading: Accolades
sections.wikitext: The track was ranked number 98th on the [[Triple J Hottest 100, 1999|Triple J Hottest 100 of 1999]], Australia's largest annual music poll which is run by the [[Triple J]] station.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/triplej/hottest100_08/history/1999.htm|title=Hottest 100 1999|date=December 26, 2008|publisher=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]]|access-date=February 25, 2021}}</ref> It also ranked 162nd on Australian radio station [[Triple M]]'s list of the top 400 greatest songs of all time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://triplem.listnr.com/w/perth/the-g-o-a-t-has-been-decided/|title=The G.O.A.T has been decided|date=March 21, 2025|website=Triple M}}</ref> In 2019, ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' placed it 58th on a list of the "99 Greatest Songs of 1999".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/media/lists/greatest-songs-of-1999-top-99-8505742/|title=The 99 Greatest Songs of 1999: Critics' Picks|author=Billboard Staff|date=April 8, 2019}}</ref> In 2023, ''[[American Songwriter]]'' ranked it second on their list of Sugar Ray's top 10 songs, behind only "[[Fly (Sugar Ray song)|Fly]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://americansongwriter.com/the-top-10-sugar-ray-songs/|title=The Top 10 Sugar Ray Songs|first=Jacob|last=Uitti|date=January 10, 2023|website=American Songwriter}}</ref>
sections.text: The track was ranked number 98th on the Triple J Hottest 100 of 1999, Australia's largest annual music poll which is run by the Triple J station. It also ranked 162nd on Australian radio station Triple M's list of the top 400 greatest songs of all time. In 2019, Billboard placed it 58th on a list of the "99 Greatest Songs of 1999". In 2023, American Songwriter ranked it second on their list of Sugar Ray's top 10 songs, behind only "Fly".
